pr.title: coverage: Memoize and simplify counter expressions
pr.description:
When creating coverage counter expressions as part of coverage instrumentation, we often end up creating obviously-redundant expressions like `c1 + (c0 - c1)`, which is equivalent to just `c0`.

To avoid doing so, this PR checks when we would create an expression matching one of 5 patterns, and uses the simplified form instead:
- `(a - b) + b` → `a`.
- `(a + b) - b` → `a`.
- `(a + b) - a` → `b`.
- `a + (b - a)` → `b`.
- `a - (a - b)` → `b`.

Of all the different ways to combine 3 operands and 2 operators, these are the patterns that allow simplification.

(Some of those patterns currently don't occur in practice, but are included anyway for completeness, to avoid having to add them later as branch coverage and MC/DC coverage support expands.)

---

This PR also adds memoization for newly-created (or newly-simplified) counter expressions, to avoid creating duplicates.

This currently makes no difference to the final mappings, but is expected to be useful for MC/DC coverage of match expressions, as proposed by https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/124278#issuecomment-2106754753.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: No source-grounded semantic counterexample exists for PR #125106. The historical `InstrumentCoverage::make_expression` change only memoizes structurally identical counter expressions and rewrites five algebraically valid forms: `(a - b) + b => a`, `(a + b) - b => a`, `(a + b) - a => b`, `a + (b - a) => b`, and `a - (a - b) => b`. These replacements are mathematically equal for all counter values, including modular/wrapping counter arithmetic, and the PR itself describes the old behavior as redundant but equivalent, not a miscompile. The observed `.cov-map` and MIR diff changes are reductions in expression-table entries and mappings, not changes in instrumented program values. Constructing a pair that differs numerically would require an unrelated or artificial return-value change, which the task forbids.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `CoverageCounters::make_expression` unconditionally created a new expression node for every requested combination: `let expression = Expression { lhs: lhs.as_term(), op, rhs: rhs.as_term() };` followed by `let id = self.expressions.push(expression);`. The expression table therefore retained redundant nested forms such as `(a - b) + b`, `(a + b) - b`, `(a + b) - a`, `a + (b - a)`, and `a - (a - b)`, even when those equal a single operand.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, when `InstrumentCoverage` requested a counter expression matching one of the five algebraic identities, the pass emitted and referenced a fresh `Expression` node for the combined form instead of returning the equivalent existing `BcbCounter`. Example from the supplied regression expectations: `false = ((c1 + c2) - c2)` was previously used at a branch/mapping, while the corrected output is `false = c1`. This was an expression-redundancy/optimization missed transformation, not a semantic miscompile; the PR is titled "Memoize and simplify counter expressions" and describes avoiding "obviously-redundant expressions like `c1 + (c0 - c1)`, which is equivalent to just `c0`."
analysis.inputDomain: Coverage-instrumented Rust functions where `InstrumentCoverage` builds coverage counter expressions from BCB counters and edges, especially nested branch/while/if/lazy-boolean/closure/async coverage graphs. The relevant inputs are requests to combine two `BcbCounter` operands with `Op::Add`/`Op::Subtract` where one operand is itself an `Expression` and the two-level tree matches one of the five identities. Construct paired MIR/cov-map inputs differing only in whether the expression builder requests the nested algebraic form or directly reuses the equivalent counter.
analysis.summary: `InstrumentCoverage` counter-expression construction should algebraically simplify the five size-3/two-operator patterns and memoize structurally identical expressions. This historical PR changed the pass from unconditionally pushing a new nested `BcbExpression` to returning the existing operand for `(a - b) + b`, `(a + b) - b`, `(a + b) - a`, `a + (b - a)`, and `a - (a - b)`, preventing redundant coverage expressions. The changed coverage `.cov-map` files and MIR dumps show nested expressions being replaced by the simplified counter.
analysis.trigger: The trigger is a new coverage counter-expression request whose operands form one of the five simplifiable patterns, for example a branch target computed as `(c1 + c2) - c2`, or `false = c1` after simplification in `tests/coverage/branch/while.cov-map`.
preconditions: The caller is `CoverageCounters::make_expression` within coverage instrumentation.
The requested expression has a `BcbCounter::Expression` operand on the relevant side, and its `op`, `lhs`, and `rhs` match one of the five identities.
Expression IDs index `IndexVec<ExpressionId, BcbExpression>`; simplification must return an existing `BcbCounter` without pushing an expression node.
Memoization keys use the hashable/equality-comparable structural `BcbExpression { lhs, op, rhs }` and return the same `BcbCounter` for repeated requests.
pitfalls: Do not treat the old redundant expression as a semantic bug; it was mathematically equivalent but wasteful.
Do not attach the downstream `CleanupPostBorrowck` test-dump changes as a separate optimization of that pass; those dumps changed because the input InstrumentCoverage expressions were simplified.
The simplification must occur before pushing a new expression: otherwise the redundant node is still interned even if callers later use the simplified counter.
Memoization is structural and keyed by the requested `BcbExpression`; `BcbCounter` and `BcbExpression` needed `PartialEq`, `Eq`, and `Hash` support for this.

`into_expressions` asserts that converting internal `BcbExpression` records to public `Expression` records preserves vector length: `assert_eq!(old_len, expressions.len());`, because expression IDs are indexes.
analysis.testStrategy: Use coverage UI tests that inspect `.cov-map` expression tables and MIR-opt coverage dumps. Add/adjust programs exercising `if`, `while`, lazy boolean, closures, async, and branch coverage so the instrumentor requests patterns such as `(c1 + c2) - c2`. Verify the resulting `.cov-map` has fewer expressions and mappings reference `Counter(1)` instead of a redundant `Expression(... Sub ...)`; also verify `tests/mir-opt/coverage/*.InstrumentCoverage.diff` and `*.CleanupPostBorrowck.diff` no longer contain the removed expression. Preserve one case per simplifiable pattern if constructing focused synthetic coverage-expression tests; no compiler execution is claimed here.
